questions.q: Do you know your neighbours well?
questions.answer: Reasonably well, yes. In our building people are fairly friendly, so we greet each other and occasionally chat. I wouldn't say we're close, but there's a warm, [[cordial]] relationship, which matters when you live so near people.

questions.q: How often do you see your neighbours?
questions.answer: Almost every day, just in passing, on the stairs or near the entrance, and we usually exchange a quick greeting. During Eid, though, we visit each other properly and share food, which is a [[heartwarming]] custom.

questions.q: Do you ever help your neighbours?
questions.answer: Now and then, yes. There's an elderly man on our floor, so I sometimes carry his shopping upstairs or help with small errands. It's only a small gesture, but I think these acts of [[goodwill]] matter in a community.

questions.q: What do you think makes a good neighbour?
questions.answer: Someone who's respectful and considerate, really. A good neighbour keeps the noise down, says hello and is willing to lend a hand in an emergency, but also respects your privacy and doesn't [[pry]].

questions.q: Do you think people are as close to their neighbours as they used to be?
questions.answer: Not really, especially in bigger cities. When I was younger, neighbours would drop in unannounced for tea. Nowadays people are busier and more private, so those bonds have [[eroded]] somewhat.
